acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-01 — A new workspace package @personal-events/claude-code builds, lints, and tests under the monorepo toolchain and depends on @personal-events/core (AWE-153) and @personal-events/event-model (AWE-150). It is pure: no @aws-sdk/*, no node:fs, no network, no logging side effects.

verification.definingInputProperty: The built package and its full test suite
verification.assertions: Build emits dist with types; tests pass
No I/O import of any kind — the purity half of the criterion

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-02 — effect-Schema validators, exemplar-driven from real captured Claude Code hook payloads, for the hook envelope and the consumed events — at minimum Stop, Notification, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd — including the common fields (session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name). A malformed payload yields a typed Either Left carrying a readable message; an unknown hook_event_name is NOT rejected — it decodes through a permissive catch-all member and reaches the default classification.

verification.definingInputProperty: A payload whose hook_event_name is genuinely outside the consumed set (e.g. PreToolUse) with otherwise-valid common fields
verification.assertions: decodeHookEvent returns Right, not Left, and the value carries the raw hook_event_name

verification.definingInputProperty: A genuinely malformed payload missing a required common field such as session_id
verification.assertions: Returns Left with a readable TreeFormatter message — the counterexample proving the schema is not simply permissive

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-03 — A source: "claude-code" mapping config JSON, schema-validated against core's mapping-config schema, keyed most-specific-first with a documented default rule. The shipped defaults reflect intent: Notification+permission_prompt → alert priority 6; Notification+idle_prompt → alert priority 5; Stop → notification priority 2 (so per-turn completions do not flood the bucket); unmatched → notification priority 3.

verification.definingInputProperty: One real exemplar per shipped rule, including BOTH Notification subtypes since they classify differently
verification.assertions: Each exemplar resolves to exactly the documented eventType and priority; the test enumerates every shipped rule and fails if a rule is added without a case

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-04 — A pure normalizer that, given a decoded hook payload, produces the NormalizedEvent shape core consumes: a human-readable name (prompt-complete, agent-waiting, …), the source, an event identity for dedupe, the project derived from cwd, and a transcript reference. It drops noise (events outside the consumed set), takes only the field slices it needs, and performs no I/O.

verification.definingInputProperty: Each consumed-event exemplar plus at least one event outside the consumed set
verification.assertions: Field extraction matches expectations for every consumed event; the out-of-set event is dropped rather than crashing or emitting

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-05 — Every name the package can emit satisfies event-model's NoDotString (/^[^.]+$/), including the default kebab derivation for an unknown hook_event_name — a hook event containing a dot must not produce an unparseable S3 key.

verification.definingInputProperty: An unknown hook_event_name that CONTAINS A DOT (e.g. Custom.Thing), exercising the derived default rather than the fixed table values
verification.assertions: The derived name matches /^[^.]+$/ and is accepted by event-model's NoDotString schema. The fixed table values satisfy this trivially, so only the derived-default path can disprove it

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-06 — Changing an event's classification or priority is a JSON edit only, requiring no code change; the config schema rejects unknown shapes and out-of-range priorities.

verification.definingInputProperty: A modified copy of the config JSON with one rule's priority changed, and a tampered copy with priority 9
verification.assertions: Classification changes with no source edit; the out-of-range priority is rejected by the schema

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-07 — Unit tests, driven by the exemplar files, cover: each consumed event decoding and mapping to its expected eventType/priority; an unknown event reaching the default; a malformed payload producing a readable typed Left; and the normalizer's field extraction and noise filtering.

verification.definingInputProperty: The complete consumed set: Stop, Notification x3 subtypes, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd — 7 cases, one exemplar file each
verification.assertions: it.each enumerates the exemplars/ directory listing so a missing exemplar fails the suite rather than silently shrinking coverage

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: AC-08 — Guidance conformance: pure Gather→Compute with no Persist, module SRP, no enums (as const / Schema.Literal), Record lookups over if/else if chains, Either results, no accumulator loops, explicit return types. Verified by biome + typecheck.

verification.command: pnpm --filter @personal-events/claude-code exec biome check src && pnpm --filter @personal-events/claude-code typecheck

verification.assertions: No TypeScript enum — a counterexample check biome does not enforce

thirdPartyIntegration.note: Deliberately none. This package is pure; its only inputs are captured exemplar files. The end-to-end S3 path is exercised by AWE-162 — Publishable hook CLI. Exemplar capture is a local activity against the developer's own Claude Code session, not a third-party API call, so no live production test and no production-write approval applies.
